text:
maya: Hey team, ACME reported their monthly tokens dropped to 0 at 00:00 UTC but some streaming calls immediately got 429s while later non-stream calls succeeded. They say UI showed 0 then jumped a couple minutes later. Any ideas?

devon: Do we have request IDs / response headers from the 429s? streaming vs normal http?

maya: Pasting customer headers from a failed stream attempt:
```
x-request-id: r-1234
x-tenant-id: acme
x-quota-remaining: 0
x-quota-reset: 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z
x-cache-node: node-7
```
They also captured server logs showing repeated 429s for the same connection.

liam: This smells like cache propagation / pubsub warmup. Our quota refill writes to primary store and publishes an invalidate; nodes then fetch new counters. If a node misses the pubsub message it can serve stale bucket=0 until it polls again (poll cycle currently ~120s). Do they use long-lived websockets?

maya: Yes — long-lived streaming ws kept open for hours. Customer said their stream stayed connected through reset and then started getting 429s mid-stream. Reconnecting fixed it after a minute or two.

devon: That matches. Node-7 in the header is suspicious. If node-7 missed seq 98123 on pubsub it would still believe bucket=0. Can ops pull node-7 logs for 00:00-00:03?

sarah: Billing confirms refill was written at 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z (UTC). No proration or manual adjustments.

quota-bot: [automated] quota refill event for tenant=acme at 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z, new_tokens=5000000, pubsub_seq=98123

liam: Repro idea: simulate a node that misses the pubsub message while client holds long-lived connection and then observe 429s until poll catches up. devon, want me to run?

devon: Please, run this script to reproduce locally: 
```
# reproduce: start stream -> block redis pubsub -> trigger refill -> watch for 429 from node
python tests/repro_quota_miss.py --tenant acme --block-pubsub-for 180
```

devon: Short-term mitigation: reduce poll window from 120s -> 30s and add explicit pubsub ACK/heartbeat on refill so nodes detect missed seqs faster. Long-term: make refill atomic by versioning the bucket and checking version on auth path so stale nodes reject stale state and fetch fresh.

maya: Draft customer message: "We're investigating. It looks like a short propagation window (up to ~2m) can cause intermittent 429s on long-lived streaming connections at monthly reset. Workarounds: rotate the stream connection shortly after your billing reset or force a reconnect at 00:00 UTC. We're deploying a mitigation to reduce the window." Thoughts?

sarah: Can we offer a one-time top-up to avoid next reset impact while we roll the fix? I'll approve 250k tokens credit for ACME.

devon: I'll push a hotfix to canary tonight: poll->30s + publish ACKs + extra logging for pubsub-miss. If metrics look good we'll promote.

liam: Ops checked node-7 logs: transient redis reconnect at 00:00:41 caused missed pubsub seq. I'll follow up with infra to make pubsub reconnects more resilient.

maya: Thanks. I'll send ACME the workaround + one-time credit and note we're rolling the canary. Please post canary plan and ETA once ready.

devon: Canary plan: us-west cluster at 01:30 UTC, monitor metric quota.pubsub.miss and auth.quotafetch.latency; full rollout target 04:00 UTC if green. ETA 01:30 UTC.

maya: Great — marking this thread resolved for now. Reopen if ACME reports further 429s after the canary. :thumbsup:
